headline.text: Alexia Monize reposted Patrick Monize's post: Not just users - creators of what’s next. Young people are growing up in a world designed to capture attention. They deserve environments that help them direct it. Preparing future generations is not about limiting technology - it is about equipping youth to understand it, build with it, and lead within it. At Braintech Robotics, students engage with technology differently - designing, programming, testing, and solving real challenges alongside mentors. This shift from passive interaction to intentional creation builds confidence, systems thinking, and long-term readiness. This March Break, we are creating spaces where youth move from consumers of technology to confident creators. Learn more: https://lnkd.in/gfxvYUMU #HealthyTechEngagement #STEMeducation #FutureWorkforce #RoboticsEducation #BraintechRobotics #YouthInnovation #BlackYouthSTEM #STEMforAll

headline.text: Suggested for you: I am 23 years old and I sell AI governance software to CISOs who have been in security longer than I have been alive. Here is what I have learned at Y Combinator: * Deep domain knowledge beats experience. When I walk into a room and can talk fluently about NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, EU AI Act risk classifications, and the specific governance challenges in financial services vs. healthcare, age becomes irrelevant. The CISO does not care how old I am. They care whether I understand their problem. * Preparation is not optional. For every meeting, I research the company's AI tool stack, their regulatory environment, recent board priorities, and their security posture. When I can reference their specific challenges before they tell me about them, I earn credibility in the first 5 minutes. * Honesty about what we do not know. I am not going to pretend I have 20 years of experience. When a CISO asks about something outside my depth, I say so and follow up with a thorough answer within 24 hours. That honesty has closed more deals than any pitch deck. * Conviction is contagious. I built this company because I saw the problem firsthand and believed deeply that it needed to be solved. That conviction comes through in every conversation. People can tell the difference between someone selling a product and someone on a mission. * The playing field is more level than people think. In enterprise software, the product and the problem matter more than the resume of the person selling it. If you are a young founder considering enterprise: do not wait until you feel ready. You will learn faster in the field than anywhere else. #Founder #EnterpriseSales #BuildInPublic

This is one of the first times we actually see it in the data
